name: Krishna
summary: The Supreme Personality of Godhead and primary focus of the Srimad Bhagavatam, known for His divine pastimes in Vrindavan, Mathura, and Dvaraka.

name: Brahmā
summary: Brahmā is the primary deity of creation within the universal cosmic order responsible for engineering the manifest material cosmos.

name: Naimiṣāraṇya
summary: A holy, auspicious forest where thousands of sages gathered under Shaunaka Rishi to hear the recitation of the Srimad Bhagavatam.

name: Śukadeva Gosvāmī
summary: The exalted self-realized sage and son of Vyasadeva who originally recited the Srimad Bhagavatam to King Parikshit.

name: Vishnu
summary: The Supreme Being and preserver of the universe, who incarnates in various forms throughout cosmic history to re-establish righteousness and protect His devotees.

name: Śaunaka
summary: A venerable sage and the leader of the assembly of rishis at Naimiṣāraṇya whose profound philosophical inquiries to Sūta Gosvāmī frame the narration of the Srimad Bhagavatam.

name: Sūta Gosvāmī
summary: A venerated sage and disciple of Śukadeva Gosvāmī who narrates the sacred discourses of the Srimad Bhagavatam to the assembly of sages gathered in the forest of Naimiṣāraṇya.

name: Vyāsadeva
summary: He is the empowered literary incarnation of the Supreme Lord who compiled the Vedas and authored the Srimad Bhagavatam to bestow ultimate spiritual knowledge upon humanity.

name: Kali-yuga
aliases: The Age of Quarrel and Hypocrisy
summary: The fourth and final era in the cycle of yugas characterized by a spiritual decline, moral degradation, and the dominance of materialistic pursuits.

name: Devaki
summary: Devaki is a princess of the Bhoja dynasty, the wife of Vasudeva, and the biological mother of Lord Krishna.

name: Vasudeva
summary: Vasudeva is a virtuous prince of the Yadava dynasty, the husband of Devaki, and the biological father of Lord Krishna.

name: Suta Gosvami
summary: He is the celebrated orator and disciple of Vyasadeva who narrates the Srimad Bhagavatam to the sages gathered in the forest of Naimiṣāraṇya.

name: Nara-Narayana
summary: Nara and Narayana are the twin-sage incarnations of the Supreme Lord who perform eternal penance in the sacred forest of Badarikashrama for the welfare of all living beings.

name: Sarasvati
summary: Sarasvati is the divine goddess of wisdom, learning, music, and the arts, often invoked as the source of inspiration for Vedic scholars and musicians.

name: Viṣvaksena
summary: Viṣvaksena is the commander-in-chief of the forces of Lord Viṣṇu in the spiritual realm of Vaikuṇṭha, serving as the divine overseer and executor of the Lord's will.

name: Karma
summary: Any physical or mental action (especially materially motivated or "fruitive" labor), as well as the universal law of cause and effect where the reactions to those actions bind one to future conditions in the material world.

name: Bhāgavata
summary: A term referring to both the devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the sacred scriptures, such as the Srimad Bhagavatam, which detail the pastimes and glories of the Divine.
